subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A herd of giraffes lives where food is high in the trees. Over many generations, longer necks become common. The best explanation is that:
options: The trees caused the necks to grow
Giraffes stretched their necks and passed this on
All giraffes decided to grow longer necks
Giraffes with longer necks survived better and reproduced, passing on the alleles
questions.explain: Natural selection: giraffes with naturally longer necks reached more food, survived and passed on those alleles.

questions.q: Which pair of sex chromosomes is found in a typical human male?
questions.explain: Human males have XY sex chromosomes, while females have XX.

questions.q: Which of these shows genetic variation rather than environmental variation?
options: A footballer's strong leg muscles from training
A plant grown in shade being taller and thinner
A person being tanned after sunbathing
questions.explain: Blood group is determined entirely by genes (genetic variation); the others are influenced by the environment.

questions.q: A gene is best defined as:
options: A short section of DNA that codes for a protein
questions.explain: A gene is a small section of DNA on a chromosome that codes for a particular protein/characteristic.

questions.q: Extinction occurs when:
options: A species becomes endangered but survives
No individuals of a species remain alive anywhere
A species temporarily moves to a new area
questions.explain: Extinction is when there are no remaining individuals of a species left alive.

questions.q: What is the genome of an organism?
options: The entire genetic material of that organism
questions.explain: The genome is the entire genetic material (all the DNA) of an organism.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of variation caused mostly by the environment?
questions.explain: A scar is an environmental (acquired) variation, not caused by genes.

questions.q: Selective breeding (artificial selection) involves:
options: Humans choosing organisms with desired traits to breed together
Letting nature choose which organisms survive
questions.explain: In selective breeding humans choose parents with desirable characteristics to breed over many generations.

questions.q: Identical twins have the same genes but can still show small differences. These differences are caused by:
questions.explain: Identical twins share the same genotype, so any differences between them are due to environmental factors.

questions.q: DNA is described as a polymer with what overall shape?
questions.explain: DNA is a double helix, two strands twisted together, made of repeating nucleotide units (a polymer).

questions.q: Sickle cell disease is an inherited disorder caused by a recessive allele. A person who is a carrier:
options: Has one allele for it but does not show the disease, and can pass it on
Has the disease but cannot pass it on
Always shows symptoms of the disease
questions.explain: A carrier is heterozygous: they carry one recessive allele without showing the disorder but can pass it to offspring.

questions.q: What is the difference between genotype and phenotype?
options: Genotype is the alleles present; phenotype is the physical characteristics
They mean exactly the same thing
Genotype is the physical appearance; phenotype is the alleles
questions.explain: Genotype is the combination of alleles, while phenotype is the observable characteristic produced.

questions.q: A recessive allele is only expressed in the phenotype when:
options: It is paired with a dominant allele
questions.explain: A recessive allele is only shown when both alleles are recessive, as a dominant allele would mask it.

questions.q: A potential concern about GM crops is that:
options: Transplanted genes might spread to wild plants, and long-term effects are uncertain
They can never increase crop yields
They make crops grow more slowly always
They cannot be eaten at all
questions.explain: Concerns about GM crops include genes spreading to wild populations and uncertain long-term health/ecological effects.

questions.q: How does meiosis differ from mitosis?
options: Meiosis halves the chromosome number and makes varied gametes; mitosis makes identical diploid cells
Mitosis makes gametes; meiosis makes body cells
questions.explain: Meiosis halves chromosome number to form varied gametes, whereas mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid cells.

questions.q: Which of these is a key part of natural selection?
options: All organisms in a species being identical
Organisms choosing to change to suit their environment
Characteristics changing only within one lifetime
Individuals with advantageous variations are more likely to survive and reproduce
questions.explain: In natural selection, individuals with advantageous inherited variations survive, reproduce and pass on those alleles.

questions.q: Which of these provides direct evidence for evolution?
options: Fossils showing how organisms have changed over time
questions.explain: Fossils show how species have gradually changed over millions of years, providing evidence for evolution.

questions.q: One disadvantage of selective breeding is that it:
options: Can reduce genetic variation, increasing the risk of disease
questions.explain: Selective breeding reduces variation (inbreeding), making organisms more vulnerable to disease.

questions.q: In the binomial naming system, an organism is named using its:
questions.explain: Binomial names use the genus (first, capitalised) and species (second), e.g. Homo sapiens.

questions.q: Carl Linnaeus classified living things into groups starting with the largest, the kingdom. Which order is correct (largest to smallest)?
options: Species, genus, family, order, class, phylum, kingdom
Kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species
questions.explain: The Linnaean order from largest to smallest is kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.

questions.q: Which is a real example of genetic engineering?
options: Dogs bred for a calm temperament
Bacteria modified to produce human insulin
questions.explain: Bacteria can be genetically modified to make human insulin, used to treat diabetes.

questions.q: How can the development of antibiotic resistance be slowed down?
options: Not finishing the full course of antibiotics
Only prescribing antibiotics when needed and finishing the full course
questions.explain: Reducing unnecessary use and always completing the course helps stop resistant bacteria surviving and spreading.

specSource: Eduqas GCSE Biology specification; Inheritance Variation And Evolution
